thesis_breaks: Audited accounts or a trading update showing underlying cash conversion persistently below the Group’s 85%–95% target range, with ordinary dividends maintained.
GDT closing with net debt leverage materially above the c.1.3x outlook, or covenant stress disclosed in a subsequent filing.
A FY2027 profit warning citing sustained gross margin below 12% on GII without a credible recovery path.
Loss of the >10% revenue customer or a material bad-debt event against the stated £75m per-customer credit ceiling.
GDT is blocked by HSR/CFIUS, or post-close US GAAP losses persist without the guided c.$80m EBITDA, leaving the Group with 1.3x+ leverage and no earned accretion.
The £502.2m customer is lost and the GP impact proves material rather than “considerably lower”.
Organic FY2027 underlying operating profit falls versus the high-single-digit guide after the FY2025–FY2026 surge.
Filing FCF covers ordinary dividends below 1.0×, or the ordinary DPS is cut (the FY2026 interim was 9.9p, up from 8.9p).
Covenant leverage at or above 3.0× or sustained breach of banking covenants disclosed in a primary filing.
FY statutory free cash flow (or OCF−capex) falling below total cash dividends such that progressive 4.8p policy is explicitly withdrawn or cut.
H1/FY revenue or underlying operating profit materially below Board guidance (e.g. loss of Data Centre momentum after normalised supply conditions).
Materialisation of Kepler SignalTek tax exposure well above the $8.7m accrued share, with a stated P&L or cash impact in regulated accounts.
Filing disclosure that the leading hyperscale Data Centre customer has been lost, or Data Centre revenue falls below the H1 FY2027 normalised run-rate without offset from other end-markets.
Statutory OCF−CapEx dividend cover falling below 1.0×, or an announced interim or final dividend cut.
Covenant leverage moving towards the 3.0× facility limit after further acquisitions or buybacks (H1 FY2027 expected no more than 1.2× after KST; statutory H1 accounts are not in this pack).
A disclosed single-customer revenue share that would make the “diversified five end-market” case unsupportable (largest-customer percentage is unknown in these files).
FY filing shows covenant net debt/underlying EBITDA persistently above the 1.5× top of management’s target range, without a credible deleveraging plan.
Order book falls materially below £1bn with management citing weaker construction end-markets in a trading update or interim.
Full-year filing free cash flow fails to cover dividends (cover below 1.0× on the Group’s adjusted free-cash-flow definition).
Confirmed material downturn in North American foundations volumes reversing H1 2026 growth, with statutory profit warning.

Full-year free cash flow covering cash dividends below 1.0×, or an announced interim dividend cut, reversing the dividend-family pass (H1 2026 FCF of £16.4m already did not cover £35.7m dividends paid).
Board withdrawal of the July/August FY 2026 upgrade, or a sharp contraction in the order book from the c.£2.4bn I-40-inflated level, consistent with a construction-market downturn.
Material losses, disputes or impairments on the I-40 programme (c.$1bn secured; c.10% complete; three to four years remaining) that reverse North America margins.
Net debt/EBITDA moving above the 3.0× covenant (0.1× at 30 June 2026), or a going-concern qualification.
Confirmed statutory FY loss or material dividend cut with FCF/dividend cover sustained below 1.0× on filing cash flows.
Castrol or other guided divestments fail to complete, leaving net debt above stated $14–18bn targets through 2027.
Further board or senior leadership disruption beyond the May 2026 chair removal, with disclosed governance or conduct findings.
Transition/low-carbon impairments materially above the 3Q26 $3.0–4.5bn guide, alongside repeated statutory EPS weakness vs underlying RC profit.
A dividend cut versus the 2Q26 8.66 cents rate, or filing FCF (operating cash flow less total capital expenditure) covering dividends below 1.0×.
The Castrol sale failing to complete, so the c.$6 billion of debt-reduction proceeds are not received.
A further chair, CEO or board-level governance event after the 26 May 2026 removal of Albert Manifold.
Net debt remaining at or above the FY2025 $22.2 billion level instead of falling toward the $14–18 billion end-2027 target (3Q26 guide $13.5–14.5 billion was a trading-statement estimate only).
FY continuing statutory FCF (SEC OCF−PP&E capex) falls below common dividends paid for a full year, with no credible adjustment narrative in the supplied filings.
Reported total debt rises further or refinancing terms deteriorate while cash remains in the high-hundreds of millions against multi-billion current maturities (per interim balance sheets).
Goodwill/intangible impairment or integration charges materially impair equity after the goodwill step-up to ~$25bn (Sep 2026 10-Q).
A disclosed regulatory or litigation matter in subsequent filings requires material restatement or sustained margin compression not reflected in the supplied period.
A Banking-segment goodwill impairment, which the 10-Q already flags as possible if the ~7% fair-value cushion closes.
Quarterly dividend cut, or trailing FCF (OCF less PP&E and software) covering cash dividends at below 1.0× once Worldpay sale-tax cash and integration spend are through.
Failure to reduce gross leverage toward the stated ~2.8× target, or a ratings/liquidity event on the $20.8bn stack (including $3.9bn of commercial paper).
Issuer Solutions integration missing expected synergies while pro forma revenue growth stalls below the updated 3.1–3.6% band.
FY2026 10-K or XBRL shows **negative** operating cash flow or FCF again, as in FY2024–FY2025 (`sec_companyfacts.json`).
Filing discloses loss of a **>10% net-revenue customer** or a material ASP/margin collapse in NAND, consistent with cited risk-factor language.
Leverage Ratio** covenant breach or inability to refinance the **$1,500.0 million** revolving facility on disclosed terms (`filings/bodies/f8854f1dddbdc4f5.txt`).
Material **goodwill/intangible impairment** or restatement tied to post–Western Digital separation reporting (`filings/bodies/123a23a80ce2b531.txt` separation narrative).
A NAND down-cycle that returns statutory OCF−CapEx negative, as in FY2023 (−$932m), FY2024 (−$475m) and FY2025 (−$120m) in `sec_companyfacts.json`.
Flash Ventures expiry, dissolution or a Kioxia supply failure that cuts wafer output the company is contractually required to take from the ventures.
Loss or sharp volume cut from the two customers that were each 12% of Q1 FY2027 net revenue, or a material ASP collapse with another underutilization/inventory charge of the FY2025 type.

Recurrence of large goodwill or inventory impairments (Yahoo FY2025 impairment of capital assets $1.83bn is unverified in truncated 10-K bodies) that reverse the peak-cycle ROE the quality models used.
Two consecutive fiscal years with filing-derived FCF (OCF minus PP&E capex) below cash dividends paid on the same statutory basis.
New SEC/DOJ enforcement or material restatement tied to intersegment or segment reporting beyond the January 2026 settlement disclosed in sources.
Nine-month or full-year operating cash flow trending toward levels that no longer cover dividends and maintenance capex without rising net debt (not observed in FY2025 10-K).
Sustained GAAP EPS and operating profit decline alongside negative working-capital-driven OCF without disclosed one-off reversals in SEC interim filings.
A full-year period in which statutory FCF (OCF − PP&E capex) stays below 1.0× dividends paid and the Board cuts or suspends the dividend.
An SEC/DOJ resolution or further restatement that imposes a material fine, additional control failure, or restatement of 2025–26 results.
A reversal of U.S. biofuel policy (including Section 45Z / RVO) that collapses crush and ethanol margins after the 2026 guidance raises.
Loss of investment-grade ratings sufficient to shut the commercial-paper market, given working-capital intensity and the negative outlook already disclosed.
FY27 average realised spodumene price sustained materially below unit operating cost (CIF/FOB) disclosed in successive quarters, driving negative underlying EBITDA as in FY25.
Liquidity falls meaningfully below committed P2000/growth capex and debt service without an equity raise (cash plus undrawn facilities no longer covering stated investment pipeline).
Material downward revision to Pilgangoora Ore Reserves or P2000 production schedule in a subsequent ASX reserve/resource or guidance update.
Statutory operating cash flow consistently below net profit over multiple reporting periods (reinstating screen Piotroski “OCF > earnings” failures on a filing basis).
Realised spodumene prices remaining at or below FY26 FOB unit cost ($569/t) for a sustained period while P2000, enhancing infrastructure and PPA connection spend is already committed.
FY27 operating cash flow failing to cover guided capex of A$1,130–1,195M, forcing dilutive equity or a breach of the stated capital-management framework.
A restated P2000 study showing incremental NPV is negative at then-prevailing SC6 prices rather than the US$1,620/t consensus used at FID.
Return to an FY25-style statutory loss with the restored 5cps dividend cancelled or cut.
Regulatory or shareholder failure blocking AliGroup close on disclosed terms, or debt drawn without expected synergies.
Two consecutive quarters of negative filing free cash flow while the quarterly dividend is maintained without balance-sheet support.
Sustained LME aluminium/alumina weakness driving adjusted EBITDA materially below Q3 2026 run-rate ($789M) in subsequent filed quarters.
Material increase in adjusted net debt above Sep-2026 levels ($969M) without commensurate earnings from closed acquisitions.
AliGroup fails to close after the September 2026 notes, leaving $2.6bn of 6.625%/6.875% debt without the acquired cash flows.
Aluminium/alumina prices reverse enough that quarterly FCF turns negative, as in Q3 2025 ($(66) million in the 8-K table), and the USD 0.10 dividend is cut.
A competition, foreign-investment or mining-permit condition blocks Worsley/Boddington or the Transaction on terms that strand the pre-funded cash.
Post-close, the up to US$750m contingent cash plus assumed rehabilitation of approximately US$1.2B crystallises into a downturn that lifts leverage beyond covenant or refinancing capacity.
Board cuts dividends below the stated 50–80% underlying NPAT policy without a matching commodity-price shock disclosed in filings.
Gearing stays above the 10–20% target through FY2027 as Louisiana LNG capex ramps without offsetting partner cash or asset sales.
FY2026–FY2027 statutory operating cash flow minus capital expenditure stays negative while payouts remain at ~80% of underlying NPAT.
Material impairment or cost overrun on Scarborough, Trion, or Louisiana LNG disclosed in a subsequent interim or annual report.
Scarborough first LNG cargo slips beyond 2026, or a material cost/schedule break is disclosed on Trion or Louisiana LNG (first LNG targeted 2029; Woodside net capex $9.9bn).
A subsequent dividend is set at the 20% of adjusted operating cash flow floor at a level below the HY26 57 US cps interim, or an interim cut is announced.
Gearing moves further above the 10–20% band with a downgrade from the stated Moody’s Baa1 / S&P BBB+ ratings.
Partner contributions on Louisiana LNG cease or reverse, so company-adjusted FCF remains negative while the $4.0–4.5bn 2026 capex guidance is spent.
Filed annual FCF falling below cash dividends for two consecutive fiscal years without a disclosed, sustainable funding plan
Disclosure that a single customer above ~14% of revenue materially reduced or ended purchases, with no offsetting volume elsewhere
Public statement of debt covenant breach, inability to service indebtedness, or suspension/cut of the quarterly dividend despite prior guidance
Failure to meet BIS settlement payment timing or a material new U.S./China export restriction on products or rare-earth supply called out in filings
A full fiscal year in which statutory OCF−PP&E capex falls below dividends paid (cover under 1.0×), as utilisation charges in FY2023–24 showed is possible.
Loss, multi-quarter deferral or export-block of the customer that was about 14% of FY2026 revenue, without an offsetting hyperscale win.
Failed or delayed HAMR/Mozaic qualification that hands nearline share to Western Digital or Toshiba, or a step-change in SSD substitution in data-centre nearline.
A further BIS/export-control or tariff shock that interrupts Asia manufacturing or CSP shipments on a scale comparable to the $300m Huawei settlement still being paid.
Filed annual OCF minus PP&E capex falls below cash dividends for two consecutive years while the base dividend is maintained or raised.
Quarterly SEC ceiling-test or property impairments at a scale that routinely absorbs operating cash flow (as in FY2024 statutory FCF deficit).
A disclosed increase in funded indebtedness or covenant constraints that materially limits drilling, hedging or shareholder returns, per risk-factor language.
A cut or suspension of the base dividend despite the board’s stated $4.20 annual base increase pathway.
Filed annual OCF minus oil-and-gas PP&E capex covering cash dividends below 1.0× for a second year after FY2024, while the base dividend is still paid or raised.
A further full-cost ceiling-test impairment, as the Q3 2026 10-Q warns may occur if trailing 12-month commodity prices fall, that wipes out the 9M 2026 cash surplus over dividends.
A cut or suspension of the $1.10 quarterly base (or a retreat from the $4.20 annual base declared in February 2026).
Inability to refinance or repay the $1,548m of current maturities of debt shown at 30 September 2026 without shrinking drilling or shareholder returns.
